documentation.purpose: Measurement-specific source display labels and caveats for the measured-sources page. These are not ownership facts, external bias ratings, or measured-quality inputs.
documentation.notesScope: Entries are keyed by measured source key. The family field is explanatory metadata for maintainers; the note text is what the client displays.
documentation.editing: Keep notes short, source-specific and tied to a measurement limitation or stream shape. Do not use this file for generic regex/NLP caveats.

medicalxpress.com.note: High evidence and causal scores partly reflect research-release phrasing. They do not by themselves show independent verification of the underlying studies.

phys.org.note: Research-release phrasing can raise evidence and causal scores. Treat them as evidence of dense research claims, not proof of independent scientific scrutiny.

psypost.org.note: PsyPost often writes formulaic research-claim headlines. That raises evidence and causal scores without establishing independent verification of the studies.

sciencealert.com.note: Popular science rewriting can make research cues prominent; the score does not assess the quality of the underlying paper.

nature.com.note: The low event/action score is largely a form effect: many Nature rows are journal article titles written as descriptive noun phrases. This does not mean the underlying research articles lack evidence.

newscientist.com.note: The low evidence score often means the headline avoids formulaic “study finds” phrasing; it is not evidence that the article lacks research support.

obits.oregonlive.com.note: This measurement mostly describes syndicated obituary entries rather than OregonLive’s wider newsroom output.

seekingalpha.com.note: Earnings, transcript and market-data formats make this source narrower than a general news publisher; read the axes before the composite.

reddit.com.note: Reddit rows reflect headlines as posted or repeated on the platform. They describe reused headline text, not original reporting or verification by Reddit.

news.xbox.com.note: Xbox Wire is official platform communication, so its score is not a measure of independent games journalism.

handelsblatt.com.note: English-language cue detection undercounts German-language headlines; treat this position as non-comparable with English-language sources.

group-mashable.note: Regional Mashable editions are grouped because they substantially reuse the same articles; their measured headline profiles are broadly similar rather than dominated by one outlier edition.

group-philippine-inquirer.note: Philippine Daily Inquirer verticals and regional subdomains are grouped as sections of one publisher. Philadelphia’s unrelated inquirer.com is deliberately excluded.

group-nypost-pagesix.note: Page Six is measured with the New York Post because it belongs to the same publishing operation; the combined view is dominated by the larger New York Post stream.

dailymail.com.note: The low position is driven especially by sensational and personal framing, alongside weaker time/place and evidence cues.

mirror.co.uk.note: Sensational and personal framing is the largest negative contribution here, even where individual headlines are otherwise concrete.

kotaku.com.note: The low position mainly reflects fewer time/place anchors, less causal/consequence language, and more direct-address packaging.

wccftech.com.note: Long tech and gaming headlines often contain specifications, comparisons and reported claims. The measurement does not assess whether rumours or analyst claims are accurate.

statnews.com.note: The small sample includes recurring Pharmalittle roundup formats, so sequence and context cues partly reflect that repeatable newsletter format.

punchng.com.note: Punch uses compressed Nigerian headline conventions that can omit explicit country or date anchors because audience context is assumed; low time/place does not necessarily mean the stories lack local specificity.

thisismoney.co.uk.note: Personal-finance coverage naturally scores highly on money and consumer-consequence cues even when individual headlines also use service or search-capture packaging.

handelsblatt.com.note: Mixed German/English feed, majority German. English-language measurement cannot fairly score it.

e24.no.note: Norwegian-language business news. English-language measurement cannot score it.

lemonde.fr.note: Mixed French/English output (Le Monde in English plus French articles). Below the 80% English threshold for fair measurement.

elfinanciero.com.mx.note: Mixed Spanish/English output. Below the 80% English threshold for fair measurement.

politico.eu.note: Predominantly English with occasional French/German pieces; above the 80% threshold.

languages.documentation: Language annotations are manual judgements from reading pooled headlines, not detector output. englishShare is approximate. measurable=false means the feed is below roughly 80% English-language headlines, so the English-only measurement pipeline cannot make a fair claim about it.

obits.oregonlive.com.note: A death-notice listing service, not editorial headline writing. Notices are form-encoded public records (name, lifespan, town), so headline-quality comparison with news writing is a category error.

streamShapes.documentation: Stream-shape exclusions are manual source-level flags for feeds whose output is a structured notice or listing service rather than editorial headline writing. measurable=false excludes the feed from the ranked ordering; it is listed at the bottom of the page with no quality claim.
